definitions.gloss: evening; early night; dusk to late evening
definitions.explanation: The period from early evening until around midnight, especially the hours after sunset when it is fully dark but still relatively early in the night.

examples.japanese: {宵|よい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
{宵|よい}のうち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: You should go home while it's still early in the evening.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{宵|よい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧じゅう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{賑|にぎ}わっていた→賑わう：14235_nigiwau⟧。
examples.english: On the eve of the festival, the whole town was bustling.

notes:
A literary and traditional word for the early part of the night, roughly from dusk until midnight. While not common in casual modern conversation, it appears frequently in literature, poetry, and set expressions. It carries a refined, somewhat nostalgic tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{宵|よい}の{口|くち}→宵の口：10087_yoinokuchi⟧: early evening; the beginning of the night
- ⟦{宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}→宵の明星：20968_yoinomyoujou⟧: the evening star (Venus)
- {宵|よい}{闇|やみ}: darkness of early night
- {宵|よい}{祭|まつ}り: the eve of a festival; preliminary festival
- {宵越|よいご}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{金|かね}→金：02618_kane⟧: money kept overnight (in the proverb about Edo-era spendthrift culture)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {宵越|よいご}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{金|かね}→金：02618_kane⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{持|も}たない→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: never hold on to money overnight — a saying about the free-spending spirit of old Edo (Tokyo)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{夕方|ゆうがた}→夕方：01010_yuugata⟧: evening — the more common everyday word for the period around sunset
- ⟦{夕暮|ゆうぐ}れ→夕暮れ：07682_yuugure⟧: dusk; twilight — the transitional period when the sun sets
- ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧: night — the general word for nighttime; {宵|よい} refers specifically to the earlier part
